rule.sl:
**have** ali **has** + **been** + -ing je za to, kar traja do zdaj: **I've been waiting for an hour.** (Čakam že eno uro.) **It's been raining since Monday.** (Od ponedeljka dežuje.) Nekateri rečejo tudi *I been waiting*; v pisanju je **I've been waiting**.

Vprašanje: **How long have you been waiting?** **What have you been doing?** Zanikano: **I haven't been sleeping well.**

Pove tudi, kar se še vidi: **You're wet. Have you been swimming?**

Dejavnost ali rezultat: **I've been painting the gate.** (čas, morda ni končano) **I've painted the gate.** (končano). Koliko časa: **She's been baking all morning.** Koliko česa: **She's baked forty scones.**

Glagoli, ki povedo, kako je, ostanejo brez -ing: **know**, **own**, **belong**, **understand**, **believe**, **be** in **have** za to, kar imaš: **I've known Jack for years.** Pri **live**, **work**, **stay** je oboje prav: **I've lived here.** **I've been living here.**
rule.de:
**have** oder **has** + **been** + -ing steht für das, was bis jetzt andauert: **I've been waiting for an hour.** (Ich warte seit einer Stunde.) **It's been raining since Monday.** (Seit Montag regnet es.) Manche sagen auch *I been waiting*; geschrieben steht **I've been waiting**.

Frage: **How long have you been waiting?** **What have you been doing?** Verneint: **I haven't been sleeping well.**

Es sagt auch, was man noch sieht: **You're wet. Have you been swimming?**

Tätigkeit oder Ergebnis: **I've been painting the gate.** (die Zeit, vielleicht nicht fertig) **I've painted the gate.** (fertig). Wie lange: **She's been baking all morning.** Wie viel: **She's baked forty scones.**

Verben, die sagen, wie etwas ist, bleiben ohne -ing: **know**, **own**, **belong**, **understand**, **believe**, **be** und **have** für Besitz: **I've known Jack for years.** Bei **live**, **work**, **stay** geht beides: **I've lived here.** **I've been living here.**
rule.it:
**have** o **has** + **been** + -ing è per ciò che dura fino a ora: **I've been waiting for an hour.** (Aspetto da un'ora.) **It's been raining since Monday.** (Piove da lunedì.) Qualcuno dice anche *I been waiting*; per iscritto **I've been waiting**.

Per chiedere: **How long have you been waiting?** **What have you been doing?** Negativo: **I haven't been sleeping well.**

Dice anche ciò che si vede ancora: **You're wet. Have you been swimming?**

L'attività o il risultato: **I've been painting the gate.** (il tempo, forse non è finito) **I've painted the gate.** (è finito). Quanto tempo: **She's been baking all morning.** Quanti: **She's baked forty scones.**

I verbi che dicono come stanno le cose restano senza -ing: **know**, **own**, **belong**, **understand**, **believe**, **be** e **have** per ciò che possiedi: **I've known Jack for years.** Con **live**, **work**, **stay** vanno bene tutti e due: **I've lived here.** **I've been living here.**
rule.en:
**have** or **has** + **been** + -ing is for what has been going on up to now: **I've been waiting for an hour.** **It's been raining since Monday.** Some people also say *I been waiting*; writing wants **I've been waiting**.

To ask: **How long have you been waiting?** **What have you been doing?** To say no: **I haven't been sleeping well.**

It also tells what you can still see: **You're wet. Have you been swimming?**

The activity or the result: **I've been painting the gate.** (the time; perhaps not finished) **I've painted the gate.** (it's done). How long: **She's been baking all morning.** How many: **She's baked forty scones.**

Verbs that say how things are stay without -ing: **know**, **own**, **belong**, **understand**, **believe**, **be**, and **have** for what you own: **I've known Jack for years.** With **live**, **work**, **stay**, both are right: **I've lived here.** **I've been living here.**
